name: Neck training harness

lead: A neck training harness is a head strap or cap, attached to a chain and weight plate, that loads the neck muscles through flexion, extension and side flexion. Wrestlers and fighters have long used it, and it has gained popularity among people seeking a thicker neck.
Visually, a larger neck broadens the base of the head, affecting the silhouette and how the face and jaw sit in photographs.

paras: The neck muscles respond to loading like any other: progressive resistance, sufficient volume and recovery increase strength and size. Systematic reviews of neck exercise in people with neck pain show neuromuscular and strength adaptations, though I found no review focused on muscle thickness in healthy lifters, so the appearance claim rests on general resistance-training principles.

The cervical spine is fragile, so heavy loads, jerky reps and poor control risk strains and nerve irritation; start very light and progress slowly. People with neck injury, disc problems or dizziness should seek medical advice. Product claims about a quick thick neck are plausible with months of work, but the evidence for lifters is indirect.
